---
title: "Customer Churn Modeling with Logistic Regression (GLM)"
output: html_document
---

## 01 Data Inspection

```{r}
# Load data
data <- read.csv("Data/retail_dataset.csv")

# Inspect
dim(data)
colnames(data)
str(data)
head(data)

# Outcome check
table(data$churned)
```

## 02 Dataset Transformation

```{r}
# Select customer-level variables
keep_vars <- c(
  "customer_id","churned","age","gender","income_bracket",
  "loyalty_program","membership_years",
  "days_since_last_purchase","website_visits",
  "app_usage","social_media_engagement",
  "online_purchases","in_store_purchases",
  "customer_support_calls"
)

cust_data <- data[, keep_vars]

# Keep one row per customer
cust_data <- cust_data[!duplicated(cust_data$customer_id), ]

# Convert churn to binary
cust_data$churned <- ifelse(cust_data$churned == "Yes", 1, 0)

# Convert categorical variables
cust_data$gender <- as.factor(cust_data$gender)
cust_data$income_bracket <- as.factor(cust_data$income_bracket)
cust_data$loyalty_program <- as.factor(cust_data$loyalty_program)
cust_data$app_usage <- as.factor(cust_data$app_usage)
cust_data$social_media_engagement <- as.factor(cust_data$social_media_engagement)

# Sanity checks
dim(cust_data)
table(cust_data$churned)
```

## 03 Baseline Logistic Regression (GLM)

```{r}
# Fit baseline logistic regression model
glm_baseline <- glm(
  churned ~ 
    days_since_last_purchase +
    website_visits +
    app_usage +
    social_media_engagement +
    online_purchases +
    in_store_purchases +
    customer_support_calls +
    age +
    income_bracket +
    loyalty_program +
    membership_years,
  data = cust_data,
  family = binomial
)

# Model summary
summary(glm_baseline)
nobs(glm_baseline)
```

## 04 Model Diagnostics

```{r}
# Predicted probabilities
pred_prob <- predict(glm_baseline, type = "response")

# Basic summary
summary(pred_prob)

# Check range
range(pred_prob)

# Histogram of predicted probabilities
hist(
  pred_prob,
  breaks = 50,
  main = "Distribution of Predicted Churn Probabilities",
  xlab = "Predicted Probability of Churn"
)

# Intepretation:
# The distribution of predicted probabilities is tightly centered around 0.5, indicating limited discriminative power of the baseline logistic regression. This is consistent with small coefficient magnitudes and minimal reduction in deviance relative to the null model, suggesting that the included predictors provide weak signal for churn classification.

```

## 05 Model Evaluation

```{r}
# Choose a probability threshold
pred_class <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

# Confusion matrix
table(
  Predicted = pred_class,
  Actual = cust_data$churned
)

# ROC curve and AUC
library(pROC)

roc_obj <- roc(cust_data$churned, pred_prob)

# Plot ROC curve
plot(
  roc_obj,
  main = "ROC Curve for Logistic Regression Churn Model"
)

# AUC value
auc(roc_obj)

# Interpretation:
# The baseline logistic regression exhibits no meaningful discriminative power (AUC ≈ 0.50), indicating that the included behavioral and demographic predictors provide insufficient signal to distinguish churned from non-churned customers. This result is consistent across coefficient estimates, predicted probability distributions, confusion matrix performance, and ROC analysis, suggesting that churn in this dataset is largely unpredictable under a linear logit specification.

```
